A 59-year-old woman presents to the office because of persistent upper back tenderness and
discomfort for the past 2 months. She mentions that she works as a jeweler and spends several hours
per day hunched over her work. Medical history is remarkable for advanced osteoporosis. Physical
examination reveals a prominent left transverse process of T6. The transverse processes become
more symmetrical in extension. The patient is set up for facilitated positional release (FPR). She is
seated upright, and a downward compressive force is applied to her shoulders. The most appropriate
subsequent patient positioning is Answer Choices: (A) extension with left rotation and left sidebending
(B) flexion with right rotation and left sidebending (C) flexion with right rotation and right sidebending
(D) neutral position with left rotation and left sidebending (E) extension with right rotation and left
sidebending (F) extension with right rotation and right sidebending (G) flexion with left rotation and right
sidebending (H) neutral position with right rotation and right sidebending (I) extension with left rotation
and right sidebending (J) flexion with left rotation and left sidebending
 A. flexion with left rotation and right sidebending
B. extension with right rotation and right sidebending
C. flexion with right rotation and left sidebending
D. extension with left rotation and left sidebending

E. extension with left rotation and right sidebending
F. neutral position with left rotation and left sidebending
G. flexion with left rotation and left sidebending
H. extension with right rotation and left sidebending
I. neutral position with right rotation and right sidebending
J. flexion with right rotation and right sidebending
